entities.description: Chicago DJ and promoter credited with coining the name 'steppin''; called the Godfather of Steppin'. Oral-history account: saw a couple separate on the floor, took the mic, said it looked like they were stepping.
entities.name: Sam Chatman

entities.description: West Side native; put on steppin' events for 62 years starting at age 17; first event at the Red Top on Madison off Pulaski (50-cent tickets, ~300 index-card handbills); hosted parties at Local 399 union hall for 14 years.
entities.name: Mary Harris ('Black Mary')

entities.description: Emmy Award-winning journalist at ABC7 Chicago (WLS-TV); daughter of Sam Chatman; reported on her father's stepping legacy (2022 segment).
entities.name: Samantha Chatman

entities.description: Cultural sociologist (Emory), stepper, and scholar of the Chicago-to-Atlanta stepping community; produced 'Let's Get to Work: Chicago Steppin in Atlanta' (ECDS); moderated the 2017 Rose Library program.
entities.name: Anjulet Tucker

entities.description: Chicago steppin' legend; longtime host and producer of the World's Largest Steppers Competition with his organization Majestic Gents; passed the torch in 2026.
entities.name: Pete Frazier

entities.description: Former WLSC champion and master instructor; member of Majestic Gents for 14 years; leader of Snoop & Crew; host/producer of the 2026 WLSC.
entities.name: Stephen 'Snoopy' King

entities.description: Named in a practitioner interview as the founder of the World's Largest Steppers Contest (unverified).
entities.name: Rodney Burke

entities.description: Singer; his 1978 MCA project yielded 'Love's Gonna Last,' known as the steppers' national anthem; brother of Invictus/Hot Wax songwriter Greg Perry.
entities.name: Jeffree Perry

entities.description: Chicago R&B singer; 'Step in the Name of Love' (2003) described Chicago stepping and became an impromptu steppers anthem; national mainstream breakthrough for the dance. (Handle as a factual music-history figure; no lyrics quoted.)
entities.name: R. Kelly

entities.description: Media representative for the World's Largest Steppers Competition (2026).
entities.name: Valerie Hill

entities.description: Master instructor and popular influencer in the stepping community; hosted the WLSC 2026 pre-party.
entities.name: Andre 'Dre' Blackwell

entities.description: Photographer commissioned (with writer Fab 5 Freddy) by Vibe magazine (2002) to document the Chicago steppin' scene; photographed the V103 Steppers Ball at the Hyatt Regency.
entities.name: Dana Lixenberg

entities.description: Hip-hop pioneer and visual artist; wrote the 2002 Vibe piece on the Chicago steppin' scene ('dreamlike, transcendental, rhythmic elegance').
entities.name: Fab 5 Freddy

entities.description: Local Chicago DJ ('The Cool Gent'); community sources associate him with hosting a 'World's Largest Steppers Contest' event (unverified, possibly conflated).
entities.name: Herb Kent

entities.description: Detroit dancer praised by practitioner Josiah Burt for exceptional following; a documented woman heavy-hitter outside Chicago.
entities.name: Sherry Gordon

entities.description: Dancer praised by practitioner Josiah Burt for exceptional following ('you can throw anything at those women and they stay with you').
entities.name: April 'Cincinnati Red' Burns

entities.description: Chicago dancer/mentor quoted on old-school vs. new-school stepping rules; identifies Westside Mike as a great dancer and Rich Jackson as an emerging hybrid.
entities.name: Josiah Burt

entities.description: Chicago steppin' legend named in 1983 Beverly House footage alongside Eddie Bo Parks, DeAnna Parks, Big Mike Smooth and others (archival lead; names as documented).
entities.name: DJ Sam Chatman circle (Beverly House 1983)

entities.description: Steppin' organization of Pete Frazier; longtime host/producer of the World's Largest Steppers Competition.
entities.name: Majestic Gents

entities.description: Stepin' dance organization led by Stephen 'Snoopy' King.
entities.name: Snoop & Crew

entities.description: Organization cited by Medill (2016) as the authority for the dance's bop roots; institutional records not consulted.
entities.name: National Steppers Society

entities.description: Atlanta's steppers organization; hosts the annual Heritage Ball attracting thousands of steppers from around the country.
entities.name: Good Deeds International

entities.description: One of the first Atlanta steppin' clubs; member Kharen Fulton (d. 2016) was an avid stepper.
entities.name: Class Act Steppers

entities.description: Community-authored history page ('One Dance, One Love') holding the Bopping/Walking/Steppin' taxonomy.
entities.name: Society of Boppers, Steppers & Walkers

entities.description: Community event-listing hub for steppers sets nationwide (2025–26 listings).
entities.name: I Love Steppin (ilovesteppin.com)

entities.description: Chicago steppers day-party collective; 2026 'Ultimate Day Party' at the Grand Ballroom, 6351 S. Cottage Grove Ave. (3rd Saturdays; DJ Slique Riq).
entities.name: Debonair Steppers & Walkers

entities.description: Chicago commercial radio station (102.7 FM); reported (single source) to have begun Saturday-night steppers programming in 1989.
entities.name: WVAZ (V103)

entities.description: Chicago radio station; community accounts describe heavy play of Jeffree's steppers cuts in the mid-to-late 1970s.
entities.name: WBMX

entities.description: Kennedy-King College radio (89.3 FM); reported (single source) to have begun steppers programming in 1975.
entities.name: WKKC-FM

entities.description: Stepan's sets promoter collective running events such as the 2026 Harlem Nights Steppers Ball.
entities.name: Chicago Female Promoters

entities.description: 1997 New Line Cinema film; Chicago-set romance featuring a steppers-ball scene — a primary-object witness to the scene's 1990s form.
entities.name: Love Jones (1997 film)

entities.description: The 35th annual competition: 2026-09-19, Tinley Park Convention Center; categories beginners / old school / 60-plus / new school; $10,000 cash prizes; prelim cities Atlanta, Detroit, Houston, Los Angeles, NYC.
entities.name: World's Largest Steppers Competition (2026)

entities.description: Chicago's biggest steppin' event (2002), documented by Dana Lixenberg and Fab 5 Freddy for Vibe.
entities.name: V103 Steppers Ball (2002)

entities.description: 2017-02-23 Emory Rose Library program and ECDS short film ('Let's Get to Work: Chicago Steppin in Atlanta') with Anjulet Tucker and Clint Fluker — the scholarly/community documentation event.
entities.name: 'Let's Go to Work!' Emory program (2017)

entities.description: ABC7/WLS-TV Windy City LIVE segment with DJ Sam Chatman on the origins of the dance (2020-01-15).
entities.name: Windy City LIVE — Sam Chatman interview (2020)

entities.description: WLS-TV 2022-02-09 segment by Samantha Chatman on the DJ who coined 'Steppin'' — the citation behind Wikipedia's 1974 date.
entities.name: WLS-TV 'coined phrase Steppin'' segment (2022)

entities.description: South and West Side neighborhoods where stepping took shape in the 1940s–60s (per TRiiBE).
entities.name: Chicago South and West Sides

entities.description: Tinley Park, IL: 18501 S. Harlem Ave — venue of the 2026 WLSC.
entities.name: Tinley Park Convention Center

entities.description: Chicago: historic venue of the V103 Steppers Ball (2002); venue of the WLSC in earlier years per practitioner accounts.
entities.name: Hyatt Regency Chicago

entities.description: Chicago: historic downtown venue of the World's Largest Steppers Contest per practitioner Tracey Bivens ('raised stage downtown at the McCormick Place').
entities.name: McCormick Place

entities.description: Madison Street off Pulaski, West Side: site of Mary Harris's first steppin' event (Red Top; 50-cent tickets).
entities.name: The Red Top

entities.description: Union hall where Mary Harris hosted parties for 14 years.
entities.name: Local 399 union hall

entities.description: Chicago: 6351 S. Cottage Grove Ave — Grand Ballroom, venue of Debonair Steppers & Walkers' 2026 day parties.
entities.name: Grand Ballroom, 6351 S. Cottage Grove Ave.

entities.description: Outpost cities with documented steppers communities: Atlanta, Detroit, Houston, Los Angeles, New York City, Milwaukee, Cleveland, Dallas, Baton Rouge, Norfolk, Columbus, Gary (IN), Tampa, Jacksonville, Little Rock, Windsor CT, Huntsville, Birmingham.
entities.name: Steppers outpost cities

entities.description: 1978 MCA album track; 'the steppers national anthem' (AllMusic); local hit made by steppers' requests and WBMX play.
entities.name: 'Love's Gonna Last' — Jeffree

entities.description: 2003 single (Chocolate Factory); described Chicago stepping; impromptu steppers anthem; #1 Billboard R&B/Hip-Hop, #9 Hot 100 (remix).
entities.name: 'Step in the Name of Love' — R. Kelly

entities.description: 1971 J.B.'s single credited by community histories with fueling the 'New Bop' youth variation.
entities.name: 'Gimme Some More' — the J.B.'s

entities.description: Mid-1970s J.B.'s cut cited as a foundational steppers tune (TRiiBE).
entities.name: 'Monaurail' — the J.B.'s

entities.description: The DJ's instruments: turntables, vinyl 45s/LPs, microphone; direct-drive decks became the club DJ's industry-standard tool in the late 1970s–1980s.
entities.name: Turntables and the DJ microphone
